A precision six-jaw clamp machined from steel. The project brought CAD preparation, CAM setup, workholding, and CNC machining together in a finished mechanical component.

title: Impromptu Speech Trainer
summary: A deployed AI speech-coaching platform: record a timed impromptu speech, get per-criterion feedback from a rubric that tightens with difficulty.
description:
## Overview

Impromptu Speech Trainer is a production web application for practising timed
impromptu speaking. You receive a prompt, speak against a countdown, and get
per-criterion AI feedback on the recording — with scoring rubrics that tighten
as the difficulty level rises, so a score at hard difficulty is not the same
achievement as the identical score at easy.

Built and deployed solo.

## The record-to-score pipeline

The core of the product is a single pipeline engineered end to end:

1. **Capture** — browser audio recording in the client.
2. **Store** — the audio object is uploaded to Cloudflare R2.
3. **Transcribe** — AssemblyAI returns the transcript along with filler-word
   detection and words-per-minute analysis.
4. **Score** — an LLM evaluates the transcript against difficulty-scaled rubrics
   and returns structured per-criterion feedback.
5. **Persist** — sessions and scores are modelled in PostgreSQL through Prisma
   and surfaced as a Recharts progress dashboard.

## Engineering decisions worth naming

**Provider fallback under upstream failure.** A third-party outage during
development took the scoring path down. Rather than wait it out, I implemented
a fallback from the Claude API to Gemini, so the scoring path stays available
when the primary provider does not. This was a reaction to a real incident,
not a hypothetical one.

**Bounded AI spend.** Per-user distributed rate limiting on Upstash Redis caps
how much inference any single account can trigger. An AI feature with an
unbounded cost per user is a feature that cannot be left running in public.

**Difficulty-scaled rubrics.** Scoring criteria tighten with difficulty, so
progress over time is measured against a moving standard rather than a fixed one.

## Deployment

Deployed on Vercel with GitHub Actions CI, and a Cloudflare R2 CDN serving
audio and optimised image assets.

title: Aranya Ceylon
summary: A dual-market e-commerce platform — LKR and USD from one catalog — with token-rotation auth, idempotent payment webhooks and atomic checkout.
description:
## Overview

Aranya Ceylon is a full-stack e-commerce platform built to sell into two markets
at once — local Sri Lankan customers paying in LKR and international customers
paying in USD — from a single catalog, with market-scoped pricing and separate
payment gateways.

Built solo, as a pnpm monorepo.

## Architecture

Three workspaces: a Next.js 14 App Router storefront, an Express REST API, and a
shared Zod schema package consumed by both. The shared schemas give end-to-end
TypeScript type safety across the client/server boundary — a contract change
that breaks the frontend fails at compile time rather than in production.

## Authentication

Short-lived JWT access tokens with opaque refresh-token rotation and
token-family reuse detection: if a refresh token is replayed, the entire token
family is invalidated rather than just the individual token. All browser traffic
routes through a same-origin backend-for-frontend proxy so tokens stay in
HttpOnly cookies and are never reachable from client JavaScript.

## Commerce engine

- **Dual market.** Market-scoped pricing with separate gateways — Stripe for
  international, PayHere for local.
- **Idempotent webhooks.** Stripe webhook handling is idempotent, so a redelivered
  event cannot double-fulfil or double-charge an order.
- **Atomic checkout and refunds.** Checkout and refund paths run as transactions
  with stock restoration, so a failure mid-flow cannot leave inventory wrong.
- **Integer-cents money arithmetic.** Prices are stored and computed in integer
  cents throughout, eliminating floating-point pricing errors.

## Data layer

PostgreSQL modelled with Prisma across 14 migrations, using full-text search for
the catalog and cursor pagination rather than offset pagination.

## Admin console

A role-gated admin surface covering revenue reporting, inventory and image
management, order fulfilment and refunds, and an append-only audit log. Backed
by a Vitest regression suite running in GitHub Actions CI.

## Status

Feature-complete and covered by tests. Not yet public — the remaining work is
product photography to replace placeholder imagery across the catalog.

title: Smart Healthcare Platform
summary: Service owner for the appointment domain in a microservices healthcare platform — a concurrency-safe hold-then-book flow that cannot double-book.
description:
## Overview

A microservices healthcare platform built as a group project. I owned the
**appointment domain** end to end — the service itself plus its integrations
with the doctor, patient, payment, notification and telemedicine services.

## The hard problem: double-booking

Two patients hitting the same slot at the same instant must not both succeed.
The solution is a two-phase hold-then-book flow with defence at several layers:

- **Redis slot holds with TTL expiry** — selecting a slot takes a short-lived
  hold rather than a booking, so a browsing user cannot occupy a slot forever.
- **Per-patient hold limits** — one user cannot lock out a doctor's whole day.
- **MongoDB multi-document transactions** — the booking commit is atomic across
  documents.
- **A unique compound index** — the database itself rejects a duplicate booking
  if every layer above somehow lets one through.

The index is the important one. The first three layers reduce the probability of
a collision; only the index makes it impossible.

## Appointment lifecycle

The full state machine: hold → booked → confirmed → rescheduled → completed →
cancelled → no-show, with a dual-party attendance confirmation model (both
doctor and patient confirm) and a policy-driven cancellation cutoff.

## Event-driven integration

An integration layer over RabbitMQ with BullMQ background workers handles:

- automatic release of expired holds
- 24-hour and 1-hour appointment reminders
- waitlist auto-promotion when a slot frees up

## Operations

Containerised with Docker, with authored Kubernetes manifests and the API
documented in OpenAPI/Swagger.

title: Decentralized Freelance Escrow Protocol
summary: Milestone-based escrow smart contracts on Sepolia, validated with Foundry fuzz and invariant suites and Slither in CI.
description:
## Overview

A milestone-based escrow protocol for freelance work, written in Solidity and
deployed and verified on the Sepolia testnet. Funds are committed up front and
released per milestone rather than in a single lump, so neither party has to
extend full trust to the other.

Built solo.

## Contract design

- **Per-milestone state machine** — each milestone moves through its own states
  independently, so a dispute on one does not freeze the rest of the engagement.
- **Pull-payment withdrawals** — recipients withdraw rather than the contract
  pushing funds, which removes a whole class of failed-transfer and reentrancy
  problems.
- **Milestone-level dispute handling** — disputes are scoped to the milestone in
  question.
- **OpenZeppelin ReentrancyGuard and Pausable** patterns throughout.

## Verification

Correctness here is not something you assert, it is something you test for:

- **Foundry fuzz and invariant suites** validating contract invariants across
  randomised inputs and call sequences.
- **Slither static analysis** running in GitHub Actions CI, so a regression in
  contract safety fails the build.

## Oracle integration

- **Chainlink Price Feeds** for USD-denominated milestone pricing, so a milestone
  worth $500 stays worth $500 regardless of token volatility.
- **Chainlink Automation** for time-locked auto-release, so a client who
  disappears cannot strand a completed milestone indefinitely.

## Frontend

A React client using wagmi/viem for contract interaction, with The Graph
indexing on-chain events for history and state.

meta.status: Deployed and verified on Sepolia testnet
